//: WHAT THIS IS. The list of paper parts whose text this repository has deliberately changed and
not yet deployed, each pinned to the exact bytes that were approved and to the changelog entry
that explains them. gates/preflight.mjs check 5 reads it.
WHY IT EXISTS. Check 5 used to require every part to be byte-identical to the live service, and
check 6 requires the changelog to be AHEAD of live. Together those demanded repo == live and
repo > live at the same time, so the first legitimate correction to the paper turned check 5
permanently red — and preflight is the gate that authorises the deploy that would clear it. The
check had to keep blocking undocumented drift while allowing a documented change through, and
the only signal that separates those two is one that binds to the BYTES.
WHY A HASH AND NOT A SENTENCE. 'the changelog mentions the paper' is satisfied by an unrelated
entry. 'the changelog names the parts that changed' is satisfied twice over by a second,
unnoticed edit to a part that was already named — and since the parts are regenerated wholesale
by tools/paper-to-text.mjs, that is the likeliest accident there is. A hash is not satisfied by
anything except the bytes somebody actually looked at.
WHY PER-PART CHANGELOG ENTRIES. On the day this was written the paper had been changed by two
separate corrections landing in different parts. One anchor for the whole file would have let the
second ride on the first one's paperwork.
AFTER A DEPLOY these declarations become harmlessly stale: the parts match live again, so nothing
is demanded of them, and the pinned hashes still describe the tree. They stop matching the moment
a part changes again, which is the point — the next change has to be looked at and named too.
NOTHING GENERATES THIS FILE. preflight prints the hash of any undeclared part when it blocks, so
the value can be pasted in after reading the diff; writing it is the act of saying 'I read this
and I meant it'.
